measurements.interpretation: Single-device 20V/3A PD contract. The A12's 20V/3.25A ceiling and a 3A-class cable put ~60W here; the Y270's 65W input cap was not the binding constraint.

measurements.interpretation: Single-port input AND output up to 20V/3A confirmed with the bundled cable. 28V/5A EPR (140W) remains unverified.

measurements.source: Amazon.co.jp review, USB tester from a 100W PD charger (ASIN B0D9JHS7BQ)
measurements.interpretation: Y270 accepted ~100W initially (above its 65W vendor input rating), tapering to 50-60W as charge progressed. Same tester measured 74Wh input energy for a full recharge (~20000mAh real capacity); unit was returned. Single reviewer, acknowledged measurement error.

measurements.source: Tim McMahon POWER-Z / Gizmochina (via roadmap research 2026-11-19)
measurements.interpretation: Peak 86W (20V/4.3A); full recharge 44-46 min consuming 37.3Wh; usable output 30.2-31.9Wh USB-C (83.9-88.6% efficiency).
Measured ceiling ~88-92W at 20V/~4.5A regardless of source size; 0-100% ~93min on 96W-class, 107min on 70W.
Peaks at 30.06W via the 15V PDO - the real ceiling is ~29-30W, not 20W; the bundled 20W adapter is locked to 9V/2.2A.
